questions.q: How does Indian secularism differ from Western secularism?
answer: Secularism means the separation of religion from the state and equal treatment of all religions, but it takes different forms in the West and in India.

answer.text: In the Western, especially American, model, secularism means a strict separation, often described as a wall of separation between religion and the state. The state neither helps nor hinders any religion, and each stays out of the other's affairs. Its main concern is to keep religion and state apart.

Indian secularism follows a model of principled distance. The state keeps a distance from all religions but may intervene in religious matters to promote equality and reform, as in abolishing untouchability and allowing temple entry. It can also give even-handed support to all faiths. Indian secularism opposes not only the domination of one religion over another but also oppression within a religion.

answer: Thus Western secularism stresses strict separation, while Indian secularism allows principled intervention for equality.
